payload.rationale: Usage reports from real work in another project (2026-11-24/25), fact-checked claim by claim, showed core paths failing: the agent accept refusing legitimate orders and passing broad ones, user-corrections flooding a record with drafted answers, local mode contradicting itself, rules and patterns not reaching the agent when they matter. Making what exists work comes before adding surface. The maintainer dictated it.
payload.title: 0.1.11 carries no new feature: only fixes of gaps, frictions, performance, bugs and improvements to what exists; the features decided for 0.1.11 move to later versions, and its scope is rebuilt from the confirmed findings of the field usage reports, the open friction list and the backlog tasks that meet this criterion

fields.note: Dictated by the maintainer: "proponho uma mudança para o v0.11.0 em vez de criar novas features, vamos forca para ela somente reoluções de gaps, fricções, performace, bugs e melhorias e mais nada". ADR-717's waves are superseded once the triage maps where each moved feature goes.

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Keep the floor for chosen options and only reword the refusal", "reason": "keeps refusing short legitimate choices; the person accepts by hand each time"}]
payload.rationale: The floor, measured after "(Recomendado)" is stripped, caused 22 of 43 refusals in real use ("Sim, os dois" counts 12). A chosen option is recorded by the host itself (toolUseResult.answers), so its exact label is evidence of the person's act without needing length; tying it to the time keeps an old choice from accepting a later decision.
payload.title: An agent's accept that quotes the option the person chose holds whatever its length when the quote equals the chosen label exactly and the choice was made at or after the decision's recording; free text keeps the 20-character floor

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Accept the host's restart text as the person's answer", "reason": "opens a line that carries no proof it came from a person"}]
payload.rationale: The reader fails closed on lines that carry no proof a person typed them; the restart case is rare and the cost is one repeated sentence.
payload.title: An answer that reaches the transcript as host text without a human origin (after a restart, "Answering your earlier question…", promptSource sdk) does not count as the person's words for an agent's accept; the refusal says so, and the person repeats the order once

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Refuse a note for more than one decision", "reason": "turns a legitimate batch into many notes without closing the stale-order case"}, {"option": "Leave it", "reason": "a generic phrase keeps accepting anything in the session"}]
payload.rationale: The check never tied the quote to the decision, so one broad, repeated phrase accepted twelve unrelated decisions at once in real use. Requiring the words to come at or after the decision's birth closes that while keeping a legitimate broad order working for what follows it.
payload.title: The words an agent's accept quotes must have been said at or after the time the decision was recorded: an older order does not accept decisions born before it; one note may still accept several decisions

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Move it to the feature version", "reason": "the accidental publication stays possible meanwhile"}]
payload.rationale: The two doors writing the same note to different trees is an inconsistency that can publish by accident; aligning them is a correction, not a feature.
payload.title: ADR-700 (a note's default scope private on both doors) is a fix and goes into 0.1.11, with a changelog line saying the CLI's default changed

payload.title: The study of what an agent must know, has read and must reread (ADR-729) runs before 0.1.11 resumes, and its findings join the 0.1.11 list: what fixes a recorded failure enters 0.1.11, the rest goes to its version by the study's own reading, with the maintainer's approval

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Free text to a question never supports an agent's accept", "reason": "refuses legitimate long free-text orders that the 20-character rule already handles"}]
payload.rationale: The attack on the study found the reader treats every answer as a chosen option, free text included, so ADR-721 as built would let free text of any length through; that is the field case of a decision accepted from a misread free-text answer. Matching the offered labels keeps ADR-721's intent.
payload.title: An answer counts as a chosen option for an agent's accept only when it equals one of the labels the question offered, read from the question itself in the transcript; a free-text answer (the host's "Other") counts as typed words under the 20-character floor, and the accept's reply says the agent interpreted free text

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Only public patterns first; private ones as a count and 'read with skills'", "reason": "the private pattern still never reaches the opening"}]
payload.rationale: The cut is one over both trees, public first, so a private pattern never reached the opening (this session opened with "Patterns adopted (0)" and its private pattern left out), and patterns were the first thing cut. Patterns are few and short and govern how work is done; the field report shows a pattern known by name only and then broken.
payload.title: The session's opening puts every adopted pattern of both trees (public and private) before any decision, with the real count and a line that a pattern's name is not the pattern and is read with skills; "a public rule never drops to make room for a private one" now holds among decisions only

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "A notice after the dispatch through the existing agent mirror", "reason": "arrives after a foreground subagent has already run"}, {"option": "Wait for the action-target rules study in 0.1.13", "reason": "the field failure keeps happening meanwhile"}]
payload.rationale: In the field a pattern governing the subagent's model was known by name only and broken; nothing speaks before a dispatch today, and the existing PostToolUse mirror speaks only after the launch. The refuse-once precedent (edit-first-write-gate) already exists and is accepted practice for edits.
payload.title: Before the first subagent call of a session, mnema refuses once, naming the adopted patterns this session has not read, as the first-write gate does for edits; the repeated call passes; it is the only voice that reaches the agent before it chooses the subagent's model

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Ledger in 0.1.13; only 'N decisions changed since this session opened' now", "reason": "the maintainer wants the ledger now"}, {"option": "Everything in 0.1.13", "reason": "same"}]
payload.rationale: The maintainer chose to build the whole ledger now rather than a reduced form. Its premises (whose read a subagent's read is, whether a shell read is the agent's, what survives a compaction) were not verified by the study, so probes come before the build and their findings shape it.
payload.title: A local, per-session ledger of what the agent has read (record id, content digest, time), beside the session journal, enters 0.1.11 whole: it lets mnema say "already read, unchanged" and "changed since you read it", once per change; probes first settle how it behaves across compaction, /clear and resume, subagents and shell reads

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Only stronger wording in the existing texts", "reason": "a lazy agent skips loud text too; mechanisms are what it cannot skip"}, {"option": "Micro-functions as new MCP tools", "reason": "each tool costs context in every session of every host (ADR-703)"}, {"option": "Run B and C in 0.1.13 per ADR-730", "reason": "the maintainer wants all three before 0.1.11 resumes, to know what enters it"}]
payload.rationale: The maintainer's line of reasoning: an agent skips reading, using or looking things up because a short description makes it decide something is not for it, because a rule is not stated as a rule, and because it does not know the bench's skills exist; everything written for an agent must assume the laziest reading and impose rules, paths and descriptions. Deterministic work done by agents by hand costs tokens and opens logic gaps. Code Mode is the natural vehicle for many micro-functions without paying context per MCP tool. A comes first because it touches 0.1.11's texts directly.
payload.title: Three studies run before 0.1.11 resumes, one agent at a time, each sorting its findings into what enters 0.1.11 (ADR-720) and what goes to later versions: A, how mnema writes for and imposes on an agent that takes the easiest, laziest path (where well-written text is enough, where a mechanism such as a refusal or a gate is needed, measured rather than guessed); B, a Code Mode for mnema in both directions (the agent extracts the most from the record, and mnema extracts the most from the agent), building on ADR-551; C, a catalogue of deterministic micro-functions agents do by hand today (counting accepts, closing a task, linking to a parent, resolving a label's tree, building an accept note), exposed through B or the CLI rather than as new MCP tools (ADR-703)

fields.note: Dictated by the maintainer after his line of reasoning ("tudo que é escrito para um agente deve ser escrito pensando que ele vai tentar resolver da maneira mais facil, burra e preguiçosa possivel") and the alignment: "vamos gravar, realizar estudos e ordem, volta para as perguntas que tinha ficado via ask e depois ja dispara os estudo para ver o que pode entrar ja na 0.11.0 e o que deve ser jogado para outras versões". It adds to ADR-551, 703, 720 and 730 and replaces none.

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "A subagent's read also counts for its parent", "reason": "the parent could proceed without knowing the rule"}, {"option": "No shell read counts", "reason": "an agent that uses the CLI would be told it has not read what it read"}]
payload.rationale: "Already read" must never be said to an agent that did not read: a parent that never saw a rule its subagent read, or an agent whose person ran the command, would follow it blind.
payload.title: The read ledger (ADR-735) counts a read for the session that made it: a subagent's read is the subagent's, not its parent's; an agent's mnema show through its shell counts as the agent's read, and what the person reads through the host's shell mode does not mark the agent as having read; probes confirm both before the build

fields.note: The maintainer chose both when asked: "Só para o subagente (Recommended)" and "Só a do agente conta (Recommended)". It refines ADR-735, which stands.

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Refuse once and let the repetition pass (ADR-734 as written), measuring later", "reason": "teaches repeating rather than reading"}]
payload.rationale: A gate teaches its passing condition: one that passes on repetition teaches the agent to repeat instead of read (the first-write gate's own text says "the same write, repeated, goes through"). With the read ledger in 0.1.11 the read can be checked; the cost is one read per session.
payload.title: The gate before the first subagent call of a session lets the call through only once the adopted patterns it names have been read in this session, as the read ledger (ADR-735, 737) confirms; a repeated call without the read is refused again; one read per session, not per subagent

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Facts only in hook and refusal text", "reason": "the next step stays implicit and a lazy agent skips it; a person's rule reads as optional"}]
payload.rationale: A lazy agent does not infer the next step from facts, and does not treat a rule as binding unless it is told so. The maintainer allowed the next-step line and added: what the person defined as a rule must always be obeyed as an order; these micro-adjustments are what to watch. It replaces the "three facts, none an instruction" stance for refusals and for person-set rules.
payload.title: mnema's refusals and gate texts state the facts and end with one imperative line naming the right next step (read X with skills, ask the person); a rule the person set as a rule (dictated with always/never/from now on, or adopted as a pattern) is handed to the agent as an order to follow to the letter, not as a fact; the rest of the record's text stays fact

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Only the local-mode sentence and naming skills now; restructure after measuring", "reason": "the maintainer wants the restructured block in 0.1.11"}]
payload.rationale: The block is the only voice on hosts without hooks; a lazy agent follows numbered rules better than prose. The attack on study A showed the first draft demoted the governing_rules rule where it matters most, dropped three tools, forgot the hand-kept Gemini copy and broke two guards; the restructuring goes ahead with those fixed.
payload.title: The instructions block mnema writes into repositories (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .github/instructions, .cursor/rules, GEMINI.md and the hand-kept plugin/gemini/GEMINI.md) is restructured in 0.1.11 into numbered rules (moment, act, door, consequence), with the local-mode wording and skills named; without demoting the governing_rules rule on hosts without the plugin, keeping create_task, record_observation and resume, and keeping the lines the guards pin (or changing the guards with reason)

fields.reason: A gate that passes on repetition teaches repeating; with the read ledger in 0.1.11, the call passes only after the named patterns were read.

The maintainer chose it when asked: "Reestruturar já".

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Keep it off by default in 0.1.11 and decide after measuring", "reason": "the maintainer turned it on"}]
payload.rationale: The maintainer chose to turn it on by default; consistent with ADR-738, a gate teaches its passing condition, so it passes on the read, not on the repetition. Few rules carry an address today, so the cost lands only where a person addressed a rule.
payload.title: The first-write gate is on by default from 0.1.11: the first edit of a governed path in a session is held until the rules it names have been read in that session (the read ledger confirms), not merely repeated

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Rename skills now", "reason": "breaks compatibility with no measured confusion"}, {"option": "Rewrite the plugin skills' descriptions in 0.1.11", "reason": "no recorded failure; measure first"}, {"option": "Edit the SubagentStart text in the hook and drop the byte-for-byte promise", "reason": "breaks a documented promise"}]
payload.rationale: Renaming breaks every text and session that cites skills without evidence it confuses; the plugin skills have no recorded failure and the first draft broke a guard; the SubagentStart text tells a subagent it records, which it does not, and an option on an existing verb fixes it without breaking the byte-for-byte promise.
payload.title: Study A's smaller calls: the MCP tool skills keeps its name (the instructions say what it is; a rename only if measurement shows confusion); the plugin skills' descriptions and a fourth read-side skill wait for measurement with claude plugin eval in 0.1.13; the text a subagent gets at birth comes from a subagent variant of mnema brief that says it hands decisions back instead of recording them

The maintainer chose, when asked: "Manter e medir (Recommended)", "Medir antes, 0.1.13 (Recommended)" and "Opção no brief (Recommended)".

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Keep searching bodies and count a body shown in a hit as a read", "reason": "a snippet is not the whole pattern, so 'read' would be said of what was not read"}]
payload.rationale: The attack on study B+C found the full-text index includes skill bodies (search-store.ts:297-304): an agent could read a pattern through search without a recorded consultation, and the read-gated gates would see it as unread or be bypassed by bisection.
payload.title: mnema search finds an adopted pattern by its name and title only, never by its body; a pattern's body leaves only through skills, which records the consultation, so the gates that pass on a read (ADR-738, 741) cannot be bypassed through search

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Leave them for the label and prefix review in a feature version", "reason": "the friction stays in every session meanwhile"}]
payload.rationale: Agents hit a label that lives in both trees and got two bare ids; search hits carried no label at all, so agents resolved labels by hand. Both expose what exists to fix recorded frictions; the label must carry its tree or it reintroduces the ambiguity F5 fixes.
payload.title: 0.1.11 takes F5 and F6: the AMBIGUOUS_LABEL refusal names each candidate's tree, title and state at every site that raises it (about ten), and decision hits from search carry their ADR-n label with its tree (text, --json and the MCP reply; the host-contract weights move once)

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "Study more before any rule", "reason": "the maintainer approved the starting rules"}, {"option": "An MCP query tool first", "reason": "every MCP tool costs context in every session (ADR-703)"}]
payload.rationale: Study B+C and its attack: agents already write code around mnema, but in the shell and against the raw record, which is where the logic gaps come from; a read API with an isolated engine gives them a typed surface. The attack showed the sandbox's "nothing writes" was only convention, that a query marking reads would let a redirect to /dev/null open the read-gated gates, and that the WASM dependency and the host-native alternative were not weighed.
payload.title: Code Mode's starting rules for the 0.1.13 prototype and the 0.1.14 build: the CLI mnema query comes first and an MCP query tool only replaces an unused one, never a 28th; the agent's code runs in an isolated engine (QuickJS in WASM, the variant and how its updates are reviewed decided in the 0.1.13 study); nothing writes inside, enforced by code and a byte-for-byte test, not by convention; the transcript is never reachable; a query marks nothing as read; and the option of doing nothing on the server, leaving the hosts' own code execution to call the tools, is weighed too

payload.title: The ACCEPT_NEEDS_THE_PERSONS_WORDS refusal says how many of the person's lines and chosen options it read and the time of the last one, never their text: it helps the agent diagnose without handing it a ready quote

payload.title: Correction of ADR-728 and ADR-749 on mnema refs: the retracted mark already exists on main (each retracted row says "retracted by its author"); what agents miss is a live view, so the --live filter of issues #1315, #1328 and #1336 (no retracted edge crossed, each edge said once) is released to contributors as written; 0.1.11 keeps search --agent and --key from ADR-728, and the issue split of ADR-749 otherwise stands (#1370 and #1262 taken by us, the rest with contributors)

fields.note: The maintainer chose it after the premise was corrected: "Liberar o --live para contribuidores (Recommended)".

fields.reason: Its refs half rested on a wrong premise (the retracted mark already exists); the search half is restated unchanged in ADR-750.
Its order to rewrite the --live issues to the mark only rested on a wrong premise; the rest of its issue split is restated in ADR-750.

payload.alternatives: [{"option": "init --local in 0.1.14 as a new option", "reason": "the maintainer treats it as a gap of local mode, which already exists"}, {"option": "The gate's performance in the 0.1.13 measurements", "reason": "the gate is turned on by default in 0.1.11, so its cost lands now"}]
payload.rationale: A private decision of 2026-11-19 put local mode in 0.1.10 and it did not land; real projects run in local mode built by hand, so the missing init option is a gap of something that exists. The gate's cost grows with the record at every edit, now that the first-write gate is on by default (ADR-741).
payload.title: 0.1.11 takes local mode whole as the gap it is (mnema init --local and what the docs still call "expected"), since local mode exists in real use, created by hand; and the first-write gate's performance (T-07: it re-reads and re-parses every line of the record at each edit, with no digest or appended-suffix validation) in the performance delivery, measured before and after

fields.note: The maintainer chose, when asked: "0.1.11" for init --local and "0.1.11, desempenho (Recommended)" for the gate's performance. It adds to ADR-741.
